blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (Path traversal in read_attachment bypasses the ticket authorization check) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: CWE-22. `name` is the name the client asks for and is joined to the ticket directory as is. An agent authorized on their own ticket 7 asks for `name="../42/contract.pdf"` and reads an attachment of ticket 42 owned by another team, defeating `may_read_ticket`; `name="../../../../../etc/passwd"` or an absolute `name="/etc/passwd"` (which makes `os.path.join` discard the base) reads any file the service can open, including `helpdesk.db` with the API key hashes. Validate `name` where it enters: look it up in the `attachments` table for that `ticket_id` (allow-list of stored names) and reject anything else; additionally resolve the path with `os.path.realpath` and refuse it unless it stays inside `UPLOAD_DIR/<ticket_id>`.
findings.title: Path traversal in read_attachment bypasses the ticket authorization check

findings.evidence:
def save_attachment(ticket_id: int, filename: str, data: bytes) -> str:
    """Stores an uploaded file under the ticket's directory; returns its name."""
    name = os.path.basename(filename)
    directory = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, str(ticket_id))
findings.recommendation: CWE-862. Unlike `read_attachment`, the upload takes no `agent_id` and checks nothing: if the handler that calls it (not part of this change) does not check ownership, any agent can write files into another team's ticket, and because the file is opened with "wb" under the client-chosen name, can silently overwrite an existing attachment of that ticket (e.g. replace `invoice.pdf`). Take the `agent_id` and call `may_read_ticket` (or a write permission) before writing, and refuse or rename on a name collision.
findings.title: save_attachment enforces no authorization on the target ticket
